title: BigInteger, BigDecimal and Exact Arithmetic
summary: When int, long and double are not enough - silent overflow and the Math.addExact family that refuses it, BigInteger for whole numbers of any size, why 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3 in double, BigDecimal for exact decimal money with scale and RoundingMode, comparing with compareTo, and choosing the right type.

cards.a:
The double `0.1` is already slightly wrong in binary, and this constructor copies that exact wrong value

The result has dozens of digits of binary error. Use `new BigDecimal("0.1")` or `BigDecimal.valueOf(0.1)`.

cards.q: What does `Math.addExact` do that `+` does not?
cards.a:
It throws an `ArithmeticException` when the result does not fit

`+` on `int` wraps past 2,147,483,647 to a negative number with no error; `addExact` refuses.

`false`, because the scales differ

`equals` compares value and scale; `compareTo` compares only the value.
